To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the gut microbiota of obese individuals can be classified into different subgroups according to their responsiveness to dietary interventions, and 2) the responsiveness of the microbial community is associated with the host metabolic response.
we developed a novel approach to predict the individual response of the gut microbiome and the host to dietary intervention, and identified several microbial biomarkers for predicting this response.

“The gut microbiota of obese individuals is highly individual, but the composition at baseline predicts the responsiveness of the host and the microbiota to dietary interventions aiming to restore metabolic health.”
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a personalized dietary intervention based on the individual gut microbiota composition.
the interactions of diet and the intestinal microbiota, and their effects on the host.
the interactions between the gut microbiota and the diet, with a focus on obesity and related metabolic health.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our study provides a first proof of concept that the microbiota composition may predict the host and microbiota responses to dietary interventions in obese individuals.
the composition of the intestinal microbiome is a predictor of the response to dietary interventions.
the microbiota composition can predict the microbiota and host responses to dietary interventions in obese individuals.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the gut microbiota is a potential mediator of the effects of dietary interventions, and the responsiveness of the intestinal microbiome is associated with the responsiveness of the host metabolism.
the gut microbiota is a potential biomarker of host response to dietary interventions, and may serve as a tool for individualized dietary counseling in the future.
a diet-induced microbiota response can be predicted based on the composition of the microbiota at baseline, and that this response associates with the change of the host metabolic health parameters.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the responsiveness of both the host and the microbiota can be predicted by a microbiota signature.
the gut microbial community composition is a major factor in determining how the microbiota responds to dietary changes, and how the host responds to these changes.
the gut microbiota is a promising biomarker to predict the response to dietary interventions.
